cards.name: Alignment Guides
cards.summary: Toggles Alignment Guides: temporary guidelines that pop up while you move, draw or resize an object, showing when its edges or centre line up with nearby objects, and pulling it into line. The check mark shows the state; the command is greyed out while Snap Off is on (its enable rule needs ToolboxEnable and not SnapOff).
use_for: lining up logo parts, buttons or text blocks on a poster without placing guides
centring a headline over an image with live snapping feedback
avoid: dense layouts where the pop-up guides grab the wrong neighbour: switch it off (Alt+Shift+A) and use Object > Align and Distribute
exact numeric placement in a script: set positions in the object model instead of relying on interactive guides

cards.name: Document Navigator
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Document Navigator, the strip at the bottom-left of the drawing window with the page tabs, first / previous / next / last page buttons and add-page buttons. A display toggle only (bound to ShowPageTabs); the document does not change.
use_for: moving between the pages of a multi-page brochure, booklet or carousel
adding a page before or after the current one
gaining a little screen space on single-page work by hiding it
avoid: jumping to a numbered page in a long document: Layout > Go to Page or the Pages docker is faster
changing pages from a script: activate the page in the object model (ActiveDocument.Pages(n).Activate; IVGPages.Item and IVGPage.Activate are harvested)

cards.name: Dynamic Guides
cards.summary: Toggles Dynamic Guides: temporary guidelines that extend from snap points of objects (such as centres, nodes and edges) at preset angles while you draw or move, with on-screen angle and distance readouts, so you can place things relative to other objects without creating guidelines. Greyed out while Snap Off is on.
use_for: drawing a line at an exact angle from an existing node, e.g. 45-degree folds on a packaging net or isometric icons
spacing an object a measured distance from another by eye
avoid: busy drawings where the guides fire constantly: switch it off (Alt+Shift+D)
repeatable precise layouts: create real guidelines or use Align and Distribute

cards.name: Enhanced
cards.summary: Switches the active drawing window to Enhanced view, the full-quality display: PostScript fills, high-resolution bitmaps and anti-aliased vector edges, as close to final output as the screen allows. One of the radio group of view modes (Normal, Enhanced, Pixels ...); only the display changes, not the file.
use_for: judging the final look of a logo, poster or illustration on screen
checking smooth curves and soft transparencies before export
screen captures of a design for client review
avoid: heavy files that redraw slowly: work in Normal view and switch back to Enhanced to check
web graphics that will be exported as pixels: check them in Pixels view

cards.name: Full-screen Preview
cards.summary: Hides the whole interface and shows the drawing alone, filling the screen; a click or any key returns to the workspace. Display only; nothing in the document changes. Disabled in the page sorter and while editing in place.
use_for: a clean, distraction-free look at a poster or slide composition
presenting a design to a client on screen
spotting spacing and alignment problems away from the UI clutter
avoid: unattended scripts: the preview stays up until a key press or click, so keep it out of automated runs
previewing a single element: use Preview Selected Only

cards.name: Baseline Grid
cards.summary: Shows or hides the baseline grid: evenly spaced horizontal lines across the page at the document's baseline-grid spacing, a reference for lining up the baselines of paragraph text in neighbouring columns and frames. A non-printing display aid; spacing and colour live in the grid options.
use_for: multi-column brochures, magazines and booklets where body text in different frames must sit on the same lines
checking the vertical rhythm of text-heavy layouts
avoid: artwork without paragraph text: the document grid or guidelines are the better reference
making objects actually lock to the lines: that is View > Snap To > Baseline Grid; this command only displays them

cards.name: Document Grid
cards.summary: Shows or hides the document grid, a non-printing lattice of lines or dots at a set horizontal and vertical spacing laid over the drawing as a measuring and alignment reference. Spacing and line / dot style are grid options; snapping to it is the separate View > Snap To > Document Grid toggle.
use_for: icon and pictogram design on a regular module
laying out a modular poster, form or packaging net on even spacing
technical drawings measured in grid units
avoid: placing objects exactly on the grid: also turn on Snap To > Document Grid (Alt+Y)
pixel-exact screen graphics: use Pixels view with the Pixel Grid

use_for: web banners, app icons and UI assets whose edges must fall on whole pixels
checking the anti-aliasing of small text and hairlines before a PNG export
avoid: print work: pixel alignment does not matter at print resolution; use the Document Grid

cards.name: Normal
